2008-04-18: Sarah Palin officially gave birth to her son Trig at Mat-Su Regional Medical Centre in Palmer, Alaska.
2008-08-28: Alaska governor Sarah Palin went to bed knowing she would be tapped by John McCain to be his vice-presidential running mate.

Sarah Palin, now governor of Alaska, was mayor of Wasilla, Alaska less than two years ago, with conflicting population figures cited by various news outlets.
2008-09-02: Sarah Palin remains secluded in her Minneapolis hotel suite for a third day, receiving coaching from senior campaign aides on John McCain's policy positions and preparing her upcoming convention address.

Sarah Palin used her primetime national TV debut to defend her qualifications and experience as Republican vice-presidential candidate.
Sarah Palin made her first appearance at the Republican convention and before a national TV audience, after being embraced by the party's social conservative wing.
The National Institute on Money in State Politics published an analysis of Sarah Palin's campaign finance reports from her 2002 lieutenant governor and 2006 gubernatorial runs.

Sarah Palin is set to break her media silence with a series of television interviews, including daytime ABC news programs and a primetime special, to counter critics of her record and experience.

2008-09-15: Hillary Clinton cancels her planned appearance at a New York rally against the Iranian government after learning that Sarah Palin was also invited.

2008-09-24: Sarah Palin meets foreign dignitaries in New York during a whirlwind tour of world affairs.
2008-09-25: Sarah Palin has avoided the media for a month, holding no press conferences since her nomination and granting only three television interviews, ahead of her vice-presidential debate with Joe Biden.
2008-10-02: Sarah Palin and Joe Biden participate in the vice-presidential debate.
Sarah Palin participated in the vice-presidential debate against Joe Biden in St. Louis, delivering a performance that was seen as more confident than her recent television interviews.
2008-10-08: Sarah Palin will not hold a press conference, but has granted two more interviews to Fox News.
2008-10-10: An Alaska legislative investigation found Sarah Palin abused her powers in pursuing a personal feud against her former brother-in-law, though it concluded she did not unlawfully dismiss the state police chief.
2008-10-11: An independent investigation found that Alaska Governor Sarah Palin abused her power by allowing impermissible pressure to be placed on subordinates to get her brother-in-law, Trooper Michael Wooten, fired.

2008-11-05: Sarah Palin returned to Alaska after her vice-presidential campaign, facing fresh allegations from McCain aides over her foreign-affairs ignorance and wardrobe spending.
2008-11-06: Sarah Palin returns to Alaska after the 2008 presidential election amid public criticism and reports of internal campaign disputes.
2008-11-10: Sarah Palin gave an interview with Greta Van Susteren on Fox News, in which she blamed the media for spreading rumors about her rather than criticizing McCain campaign staffers.

2008-11-13: Sarah Palin held her first press conference since the election at the Republican governors' conference in Miami, calling for a return to traditional Republican values and promoting her potential 2012 presidential bid.
2008-11-27: Sarah Palin's interview at a Wasilla poultry farm, where holiday turkeys are bred and slaughtered, drew criticism from Huffington Post bloggers, MSNBC cable pundits, and New York Times editors.
2009-01-08: Sarah Palin appears in a web video on a conservative website, criticizing Tina Fey, Katie Couric, and Caroline Kennedy.
2009-01-27: Alaska governor Sarah Palin opens a political action committee, SarahPac, to support candidates sharing her goals and fund her political activities.

2009-03-12: The engagement of Bristol Palin, daughter of Sarah Palin, and Levi Johnston ended just over two months after the birth of their son.
2009-05-13: Sarah Palin signs a deal with HarperCollins to publish her as-yet-untitled memoirs in spring 2010.

2009-07-03: Sarah Palin announces she will step down as governor of Alaska at the end of the month.
2009-07-26: Sarah Palin resigns as governor of Alaska 16 months before the end of her term, without revealing her long-term political plans.
2009-07-28: William Shatner recited part of Sarah Palin's resignation speech as a poem on The Tonight Show with Conan O'Brien.
2009-09-23: Sarah Palin made her first major public appearance since resigning as Alaska governor, delivering a speech in Hong Kong.
2009-10-02: Sarah Palin's upcoming memoir Going Rogue tops Amazon's bestseller list, outselling Dan Brown's latest novel weeks before its 17 November release.
2009-10-21: Sarah Palin is scheduled to appear on Oprah Winfrey's television chatshow on 16 November, the day before publication of her memoir Going Rogue: An American Life.
2009-10-30: Levi Johnston says he will take Sarah Palin to court over access to his infant son Tripp, claiming Palin is preventing him from seeing the child.
2009-11-10: Sarah Palin is scheduled to appear on the Oprah Winfrey Show, followed by the launch of her book Going Rogue and a three-week bus tour.
2009-11-12: The Associated Press obtains an early copy of Sarah Palin's memoir Going Rogue, which reveals her fraught relations with John McCain's campaign aides during the 2008 presidential race.
2009-11-16: Sarah Palin appeared on Oprah Winfrey's show to discuss her new book and her life, and said a 2012 presidential run was not on her radar screen.
2009-11-17: Sarah Palin's memoir Going Rogue sold about 300,000 copies on its first day of publication.
Spoof biographies "Going Rouge" and "Going Rouge – The Sarah Palin Rogue Coloring and Activity Book" are scheduled for publication on the same day as Sarah Palin's memoir "Going Rogue."
2009-11-19: Sarah Palin begins her book-signing tour.
2009-12-05: Sarah Palin delivered a string of self-deprecating quips at a dinner for journalists in Washington, likening the event to appearing before a "death panel."
2009-12-09: Sarah Palin wrote a comment piece dismissing the Copenhagen climate conference as a political stunt.

2010-01-12: Sarah Palin announces she will join Fox News as an analyst and occasional contributor.
2010-02-06: Sarah Palin gave a speech to the first national Tea Party convention in Nashville, attacking the Obama administration and hinting at a possible 2012 presidential run.
2010-03-04: Sarah Palin's publisher HarperCollins announces an as-yet-untitled second book celebrating American virtues and strengths.

2010-05-11: Sarah Palin's publisher HarperCollins announces her new book, America By Heart: Reflections on Family, Faith and Flag, will be published on 23 November in the US.
2010-05-18: Bristol Palin, daughter of Sarah Palin, is to join the speakers' circuit, charging between $15,000 and $30,000 per appearance.
2010-05-21: Sarah Palin endorsed Republican congressional candidate Vaughn Ward in Idaho.

2010-06-15: Sarah Palin announced on her Facebook site that she hopes to secure a meeting with Margaret Thatcher, whom she called one of her political heroines.

2010-11-21: Sarah Palin dispatched aides to scope out office space in Iowa, hinting at a possible 2012 presidential run.

2011-06-17: More than 24,000 pages of emails from Sarah Palin's time as Alaska governor were released, with readers helping review the documents.
2011-06-27: An as-yet-untitled Nick Broomfield documentary offering a critical examination of Sarah Palin is reported to be screened in Los Angeles for potential buyers.
